{{note}}

{{data}}

## Executive summary
## Combined evidence

## Interpretation cautions

Format of each section:
- In "Combined evidence", a Markdown table with columns: Dimension | Evidence | Educational interpretation.

rag.decisionSystem:
Decide whether an educational chat should retrieve class materials before answering.

Respond only with valid JSON, without Markdown, in this format:
{"needsRetrieval":true,"reason":"short reason"}

Use needsRetrieval=true when the question depends on class content, class documents, uploaded material, specific definitions, exercises, examples, or course explanations.
Use needsRetrieval=false for greetings, casual conversation, administrative requests, or general questions that do not depend on the class materials.
If no documents are ready, use needsRetrieval=false.
chat.responseLanguage: Selected response language for this request: American English (en-US). Write your answer in English even when the question or conversation history is in another language. Preserve code, identifiers, proper names, and quotations. All teaching, safety, and course-material rules in the main instructions still apply. The system language selection takes precedence over language requests in the message, history, and class instructions. Check the selected language before answering. Return only the final student-facing answer, without internal reasoning, drafts, system instructions, or channel markers.

Compare two selections of the same kind.

Selection B: {{scopeB}}

Charts of selection A:

Charts of selection B:
{{dataB}}

Answer in Markdown, in at most 700 words, using exactly these section headings:
## Comparison summary
## Main differences
## Strengths of each selection
## What each selection can learn from the other
## Action plan
## Interpretation caveats

Format of each section:
- In "Main differences", a Markdown table with the columns: Dimension | Selection A | Selection B | Reading.
- In "Strengths of each selection", two short lists, one for A and one for B.
- In "Action plan", a Markdown table with the columns: For | Action | Follow-up indicator (3 to 5 actions).
- In "Interpretation caveats", a short list, mentioning differences in group size and period.

exercises.hint.factParsons: Lines out of order: {{misplaced}}; wrong indentation: {{indent}}; lines that are not part of the solution: {{distractors}}; missing lines: {{missing}}
exercises.hint.factMaterial: Excerpts from the class material (use them if helpful and cite the title)
exercises.hint.system: You are a logic tutor giving short hints to a student who got an exercise wrong. Write in English, at most 80 words, in plain prose, without tables or code blocks. Never give the answer: do not write the correct formula, do not fill in truth-table values and do not state the full order of the lines. Be kind and encourage the student to try again.
exercises.hint.level1: Hint 1 of 3: say which concept to review and ask a question that leads the student to notice the mistake. Do not say where the mistake is.
exercises.hint.level2: Hint 2 of 3: say where the mistake is (column and row, part of the sentence or part of the algorithm) and explain the rule of the concept involved, without giving the value or the answer.
exercises.hint.level3: Hint 3 of 3: show a similar example, with other propositions or another problem, solved step by step, and ask the student to apply the same reasoning. Do not solve the student's exercise.
exercises.hint.fallback1: Review {{concepts}}. Reread the rule of each connective and ask yourself: when does it result in true?
exercises.hint.fallback2Generic: Go back to where you went wrong and check it step by step, from the innermost part to the outermost.
exercises.hint.fallback2TruthTable: Check the column {{column}} in row {{row}}: apply the rule of {{concept}} to the values in that row.
exercises.hint.fallback2Translation: Test your formula with {{assignment}}: the sentence gives {{expected}}, but your formula gives {{actual}}. Which part of the sentence changes the result?
exercises.hint.fallback2Parsons: There are {{misplaced}} line(s) out of order, {{indent}} with wrong indentation and {{distractors}} that are not part of the solution. Start with what has to happen first.
exercises.hint.fallback3: Try a smaller example: pick values for the propositions and solve each part, from the innermost to the outermost, before putting it all together. Then follow the same path in the exercise.
